subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the shelf back and starry sky panel read well in the front view and the interior shading looks fine, but I'm noticing the side view shows the side panel appearing quite thin, which seems worth fixing.

The crown extrude looks heavy and dark in the three-quarter and back views due to cel-shading, though the back plain wood panel with emblem and the door moon/sun placement seem correct. I'm checking whether the leaning books on the bottom shelf overlap awkwardly with the scroll pyramid near the front, since one tilted book seems to intrude into that space.

Looking more closely at the right side of shelf 2, a leaning book angled at 14° seems to poke right at the pillar's inner edge boundary, so I'm working through the geometry of its lean offset to see whether it actually clips into the side panel.

Checking the other shelves too — shelf 1's leaning books and orb placement look fine, and the pillar depth placement at the front doesn't conflict with anything. Now I'm trying to figure out where the biggest visual improvement would come from, starting with checking the three-quarter view angle relative to the shelf orientation.

The crown's top slab thickness and centering look proportionate as-is, and the roof's flat dark brown color could use some gold trim, though the front edge already has it. Looking at overall composition, the dais is sized reasonably relative to the shelf, filling the frame well in the front view, and the lamp posts sit close enough to the dais edges to look balanced. I'm also checking the floating orb finials and loose sphere parts to make sure their positions relative to the extrusions make sense.

The crescent's orb nestles correctly within the crescent shape given its rotated geometry, so that renders well from the front, and the orbiting sparks read as intentional floating elements. For the hanging stars in shelf 3, I realize their default extrude orientation puts the thickness along the depth axis, meaning they'll appear edge-on as thin gold dashes in the front view rather than full stars.

Same issue affects the crown's pediment stars, which likely appear as similar thin dashes. The fix is straightforward: passing an explicit x-axis direction into the star() function so the thickness aligns along the correct depth axis instead. The crescent and crown extrudes already use the right axis orientation, so those are fine as-is.

Checking the remaining views, the back and side panels read fine, and the floor scene with scrolls and candles looks correct. The main remaining concern is that the dark sky panel makes the shelf contents hard to see, so adding a slight glow to the sky (around 0.35 strength) could help the books pop without losing the dark purple mood.

Now I realize the top shelf's leaning book is clipping into the side panel since its top corner extends past the inner boundary—I need to shift the leaning books on shelves 2 and 3 leftward by about 0.02 to pull them clear of the panel edge.

Good, flush at the panel face—I'll leave it, maybe nudge slightly left but it's minor. I'm bumping star sizes up a bit for visibility, both the hanging stars and the crown stars, and double-checking the crown's dark front face and pillar gold bands look right before moving to overall soundness checks.

Looking at the back view, the crown and pediment read as plain dark since the shadow cel color renders nearly black under this lighting. I could add some back-side detail like a gold frame or rune strips, but I'll skip that for now and focus on cheaper wins: star orientation, sizing, sky glow, and adding some ambient fill light since the interior feels a bit flat without it.

I'm fixing the star orientation so it faces outward correctly, checking that the hanging stars and their gold wires line up properly under the ceiling and in front of the shelf books, then adding the sky glow orb.

Adjusting star radius to 0.04 and tweaking the hanging star's size and vertical offset.
